note: A use-case taxonomy, not a legal classifier. The tier is the tier that use case normally attracts under the EU AI Act; the basis names why. A real classification depends on the concrete system and must be assessed, which is control C-04.

tiers.label: Prohibited
tiers.meaning: The practice is banned. The only compliant answer is not to run it.

tiers.label: High risk
tiers.meaning: Permitted but carries the full Chapter III obligation set.

tiers.label: Transparency risk
tiers.meaning: Permitted, with disclosure duties under Article 50.

tiers.label: Minimal risk
tiers.meaning: No specific obligations beyond AI literacy and voluntary practice.

flags.label: Processes special category or biometric data
Produces a decision with legal or similarly significant effect
Affects identifiable individuals outside the organisation
Performs biometric categorisation or emotion inference
Meets a GDPR Art. 35 high-risk trigger
Meets an Art. 27 fundamental rights impact assessment trigger
Depends on a third-party model or provider
Organisation is the provider of a general-purpose model

classes.name: Employment and worker decisions
classes.description: Recruitment screening, candidate ranking, promotion or termination recommendations, task allocation and performance evaluation.
classes.basis: Annex III(4)(a)-(b) - employment, worker management and access to self-employment
indicators: CV or application screening
Candidate ranking or scoring
Automated rejection or shortlisting
Performance or productivity evaluation
Shift, task or route allocation affecting pay
risks: Discrimination against protected groups through proxy features
Rubber-stamped human review that is oversight in name only
Candidates never told a model ranked them
No route to contest an automated rejection

classes.name: Creditworthiness and credit scoring
classes.description: Evaluating creditworthiness or establishing a credit score for a natural person.
classes.basis: Annex III(5)(b) - creditworthiness and credit scoring of natural persons
indicators: Credit score or limit produced per applicant
Application accept or decline recommendation
Risk-based pricing of a consumer product
Alternative data used as a creditworthiness proxy
risks: Proxy discrimination through postcode, device or behavioural data
Applicant cannot obtain a meaningful reason for refusal
Model drift silently tightening access
Training data reflecting historical exclusion

classes.name: Remote biometric identification
classes.description: Identifying natural persons from biometric data at a distance, including face matching against a reference set.
classes.basis: Annex III(1)(a) - remote biometric identification systems
indicators: Face, gait or voice matched against a watchlist
Identification without the person's active participation
Retention of biometric templates
Camera estate covering public or semi-public space
risks: False matches falling hardest on under-represented groups
Special category processing without a valid Art. 9 condition
Function creep from access control into surveillance
Irreversible harm: biometrics cannot be reissued

classes.name: Emotion inference at work or in education
classes.description: Inferring emotions of natural persons in the workplace or in education institutions.
classes.basis: Art. 5(1)(f) - emotion recognition in workplace and education, outside medical or safety use
indicators: Sentiment or stress scoring of employees or students
Camera or voice analysis during interviews or exams
Engagement or attention scoring from video
Aggregated mood dashboards for managers
risks: The practice is banned, so the exposure is enforcement not mitigation
No scientific basis for the inference being made
Chilling effect on protected expression
Works council and co-determination breach

classes.name: Social scoring
classes.description: Evaluating or classifying people over time from social behaviour or personal traits, leading to detrimental treatment in an unrelated context.
classes.basis: Art. 5(1)(c) - social scoring leading to unjustified detrimental treatment
indicators: General trustworthiness or reliability score per person
Score reused in a context unrelated to its origin
Detrimental treatment disproportionate to the behaviour
Behavioural data merged across unrelated services
risks: Banned practice
Cumulative exclusion with no single reviewable decision
No contestation path because no decision is announced

classes.name: Customer-facing conversational assistant
classes.description: Chat or voice assistants that interact directly with customers, employees or the public.
classes.basis: Art. 50(1) - inform people they are interacting with an AI system
indicators: Free-text dialogue with end users
Answers grounded in internal documents
Takes an action on the user's account
Hands off to a human agent
risks: Confidently wrong answers relied on as advice
Prompt injection turning the assistant against its own guardrails
Leakage of another customer's data through retrieval
Silent scope creep into regulated advice

classes.name: Generative content production
classes.description: Generating or materially manipulating text, image, audio or video for publication or customer use.
classes.basis: Art. 50(2) and 50(4) - machine-readable marking of synthetic content and deep fake disclosure
indicators: Synthetic image, audio or video produced
Marketing or public-facing copy generated
Human likeness or voice reproduced
Output published without human review
risks: Unmarked synthetic media entering public circulation
Copyright and training-data provenance exposure
Reputational harm from generated claims
Impersonation of real people

classes.name: Essential service eligibility
classes.description: Deciding eligibility for essential public benefits or services, or risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance.
classes.basis: Annex III(5)(a) and (c) - essential public assistance benefits and life or health insurance risk assessment
indicators: Benefit or claim eligibility decision
Premium or coverage set per individual
Fraud or abuse flag suspending a benefit
Health or lifestyle proxies in the feature set
risks: Wrongful suspension of income or care with slow redress
Vulnerable claimants least able to contest
Proxy use of health data
Errors concentrated in the groups least visible in the data

classes.name: Education access and assessment
classes.description: Admission decisions, learning-outcome evaluation, level assignment and exam proctoring.
classes.basis: Annex III(3) - education and vocational training
indicators: Admission or placement recommendation
Automated grading or scoring of work
Proctoring or cheating detection
Progress prediction driving intervention
risks: Life-course effects from a single opaque score
Proctoring false positives against disabled or neurodivergent students
Language and dialect bias in scoring
No meaningful appeal within the assessment window

classes.name: Safety component of a regulated product
classes.description: AI used as a safety component, or as a product, covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I.
classes.basis: Art. 6(1) - safety components of products covered by Annex I legislation
indicators: Failure can cause physical harm
Function is a safety component under sectoral law
Third-party conformity assessment already required
Operates machinery, vehicles or medical decisions
risks: Physical injury
Sectoral and AI Act conformity routes handled by different teams and diverging
Field-safety corrective action with no rollback path
Post-market vigilance duties missed

classes.name: Critical infrastructure management
classes.description: Safety-relevant management or operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or supply of water, gas, heating or electricity.
indicators: Automated control or dispatch of supply
Load, routing or capacity decisions
Anomaly detection triggering shutdown
Operator dependence with no manual fallback
risks: Cascading outage affecting many people
Automation bias in the control room
Adversarial manipulation of sensor input
Manual fallback never exercised

classes.name: Law enforcement, migration and border
classes.description: Risk assessment, evidence evaluation, polygraph-type tools and migration or asylum decision support.
classes.basis: Annex III(6) and (7) - law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control
indicators: Individual risk of offending or re-offending scored
Evidence reliability assessed by a model
Visa or asylum case triaged or prioritised
Used by or on behalf of a public authority
risks: Liberty and residence consequences
Historic enforcement bias reproduced as prediction
Affected persons often outside the jurisdiction's remedies
Secrecy claims blocking scrutiny

classes.name: Financial fraud detection
classes.description: Detecting fraud, theft or abuse in payments, claims, carrier onboarding or logistics operations.
classes.basis: Not Annex III on the fraud-detection ground: Annex III(5)(b) expressly excludes AI systems used to detect financial fraud. The tier still rises to high if the same output is reused to decide access to credit, employment or an essential service.
indicators: Transaction, claim or carrier scored for fraud risk
Alert queue worked by investigators
Automatic hold, block or account suspension
Score reused downstream for pricing or onboarding
risks: Legitimate customers or carriers blocked with slow redress
Investigators trusting the score instead of testing it
Score built for detection silently reused as a creditworthiness or eligibility input, which changes the tier
False-positive burden concentrated on small or new counterparties
Adversaries adapting faster than the model is retrained

classes.name: Internal productivity and document processing
classes.description: Summarisation, drafting, translation, classification and search over internal material, with no external decision effect.
classes.basis: No Annex III use case and no Art. 50 interaction, so obligations reduce to AI literacy and voluntary practice
indicators: Only employees use the output
No decision about a person is produced
Human always edits before use
Corpus is internal documents
risks: Confidential input sent to an external model endpoint
Quiet drift into a decision-support role that changes the tier
Fabricated content entering an official record
Shadow deployment outside the inventory
